glosses: To remove (items or material) so as to leave something unobstructed or open.

examples.text: […] Aristotle has brought to explain his Doctrine of Substantial Forms, when he tells us that a Statue lies hid in a Block of Marble; and that the Art of the statuary only clears away the superfluous Matter, and removes the Rubbish.

glosses: To leave abruptly; to clear off or clear out.

examples.text: Then the whole population cleared into the forest, expecting all kinds of calamities to happen, while, on the other hand, the steamer Fresleven commanded left also in a bad panic, in charge of the engineer, I believe.

glosses: To become free from obstruction or obscurement; to become transparent.

examples.text: When the road cleared we continued our journey.
After a heavy rain, the sky cleared nicely for the evening.

glosses: To eliminate ambiguity or doubt from (a matter); to clarify or resolve; to clear up.

examples.text: We need to clear this issue once and for all.

glosses: To remove from suspicion, especially of having committed a crime.

examples.text: The court cleared the man of murder.
[…] yet I appeal to the reader, and am sure he will clear me from Partiality.

glosses: To pass without interference; to miss.

examples.text: The door just barely clears the table as it closes.
The leaping horse easily cleared the hurdles.

glosses: To exceed a stated mark.

examples.text: She was the first female high jumper to clear two metres.

glosses: To finish or complete (a stage, challenge, or game).

examples.text: I cleared the first level in 36 seconds.

glosses: Of a check or financial transaction, to go through as payment; to be processed so that the money is transferred.

examples.text: The check might not clear for a couple of days.

glosses: To earn a profit of; to net.

examples.text: He's been clearing seven thousand a week.

glosses: To approve or authorise for a particular purpose or action; to give clearance to.

examples.text: Air traffic control cleared the plane to land.

glosses: To obtain approval or authorisation in respect of.

examples.text: I've cleared the press release with the marketing department, so go ahead and publish it.

glosses: To obtain a clearance.

examples.text: The steamer cleared for Liverpool today.

glosses: To obtain permission to use (a sample of copyrighted audio) in another track.

glosses: To reset or unset; to return to an empty state or to zero.

examples.text: to clear an array;  to clear a single bit (binary digit) in a value

glosses: To style (an element within a document) so that it is not permitted to float at a given position.

examples.text: To get the footer acting right, you need to float it and clear it on both margins.

glosses: To unload a firearm, or undergo an unloading procedure, in order to prevent negligent discharge; for safety reasons, to check whether one's firearm is loaded or unloaded.

examples.text: To prevent any shooting accidents, remember to clear your pistol and stay aware of your surroundings.

glosses: Full extent; distance between extreme limits; especially; the distance between the nearest surfaces of two bodies, or the space between walls.

examples.text: a room ten feet square in the clear

examples.text: It took me weeks to achieve a one-credit clear (1CC).
